notes: DCA 6-2015 Table 2, Maximum Joist Spans and Overhangs (p. 4), transcribed 2026-09-27 (#41 slice B1) from the PDF in the guide's sources, read from the rendered page (300 dpi) and checked against the text extraction; both agree on every cell. Rows carry the printed species group; each row's span is the Allowable Span (L_J) cell and its overhang the Allowable Overhang (L_O) cell of the same species, size and spacing. Every note is transcribed verbatim and shown with results (not-encoded); note 3's cap, 'the lesser of allowable overhang, L_O, or one fourth the joist span, L/4' (p. 3), is also declared as overhangLimit. Not yet reviewed: docs/code-packs/reviews/us-ct-2022/dca6-table2.md.

footnotes.text: Assumes 40 psf live load, 10 psf dead load, No. 2 grade, and wet service conditions.
Maximum allowable overhang cannot exceed L/4 or ¼ of actual main span. Assumes cantilever length/180 deflection with 220 lb point load (See Figure 1A and Figure 2).
Incising assumed for Douglas Fir-Larch, Hem-Fir, and Spruce-Pine-Fir.
Design values based on northern species with no incising assumed.
Ledger shall be a minimum of 2x8 nominal. Joists and rim joists to which guard posts are attached shall be a minimum of 2x8 nominal.
Joist length prescriptively limited to 18'-0" for footing design.
